name: Encrypting Messages
description: The Smart Beaver from ABBYY invented a new message encryption method and now wants to check its performance. Checking it manually is long and tiresome, so he decided to ask the ABBYY Cup contestants for help. A message is a sequence of n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . Encryption uses a key which is a sequence of m integers b 1 , b 2 , ..., b m ( m ≤ n ). All numbers from the message and from the key belong to the interval from 0 to c - 1 , inclusive, and all the calculations are performed modulo c . Encryption is performed in n - m + 1 steps. On the first step we add to each number a 1 , a 2 , ..., a m a corresponding number b 1 , b 2 , ..., b m . On the second step we add to each number a 2 , a 3 , ..., a m + 1 (changed on the previous step) a corresponding number b 1 , b 2 , ..., b m . And so on: on step number i we add to each number a i , a i + 1 , ..., a i + m - 1 a corresponding number b 1 , b 2 , ..., b m . The result of the encryption is the sequence a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n after n - m + 1 steps. Help the Beaver to write a program that will encrypt messages in the described manner.
input_specification: The first input line contains three integers n , m and c , separated by single spaces. The second input line contains n integers a i ( 0 ≤ a i < c ), separated by single spaces — the original message. The third input line contains m integers b i ( 0 ≤ b i < c ), separated by single spaces — the encryption key. The input limitations for getting 30 points are: 1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 10 3 1 ≤ c ≤ 10 3 The input limitations for getting 100 points are: 1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ c ≤ 10 3
output_specification: Print n space-separated integers — the result of encrypting the original message.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 177D2 — Encrypting Messages [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
